minutes.headline: Capital Planning Committee debated long-range planning, elected Tom Alonso chair, and set an early-October project request.
minutes.summary: First meeting of the season: members reordered the agenda to discuss budget-season practice before reorganizing. They argued over a comprehensive multi-year capital plan, estimate quality, a town engineer, and signaling out-year priorities to departments. Officers were then elected, the capital inventory was briefly discussed, and the schedule for department requests was set.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; no members of the public had joined.
Second call for public comment at close; none.

budget_items.what_was_said: School committee assessment of bringing Turkey Hill to serve 10-15 more years; excludes ADA compliance.

budget_items.topic: Engineering for Turkey Hill ADA work
budget_items.what_was_said: Questioned how to justify engineering spending just to learn whether work can be done, versus buying a cruiser.
Discussion of whether to invest in Brooks house requests that rank low every year; fiscal 25 items cited.
Public resistance to paying for engineering feasibility work.
A member suggested moving vehicles into the operating budget rather than capital.
Proposed ranking scheme tied to town manager's projected available capital funds.

decisions.decision: Use the same evaluation criteria and scoring as last year for department capital requests.
Requests go out for return around the first week of October; next meeting first week of October; presentations to follow about the third week.
Review the capital inventory of assets at the next meeting.
Ask departments to use a standardized presentation format (e.g., PowerPoint) with basis of estimate.
Considered a spring five-year-plan session and green/yellow/red or 1-5 out-year indicator; no formal action.

what_happened.line: Members elected a chair, a vice chair and a clerk by voice vote; the chair nominee abstained on his own nomination.
Members agreed to score department capital requests with the same criteria and scoring as last year.
Requests are set to return around the first week of October, with department presentations to follow about the third week.
Departments will be asked to present in a standard format, such as a slideshow, with the basis of each cost estimate.
Members discussed a multi-year capital plan and signaling out-year priorities to departments; they took no formal action.

why_it_matters: The committee ranks the capital requests that shape what residents are later asked to fund, so the scoring criteria and the estimate standards set which projects move forward.
Without a formal multi-year plan, departments have little notice of which projects the committee may favor in later years.
